items.section: 3.1 A me, a self's universal set, uniquenessing
items.sentence: Universal is bothboth, only one possibly now-existing and only one possibly same-existing, so a me is only one possibly now-existing, now, and only one possibly same-existing, from its prior: its uniqueness is its being universal, both ways.
items.text: Identical molecules each have their own colour, set by their neighbours, and identical nuclei are told apart by their neighbours only.
items.from: earlier item: Identical molecules each have their own colour (at Me)
